purpose: Bounded prompt selection evidence; assistant-review agreement under the documented article-association policy, not human-adjudicated population accuracy.

method.sample: 120 distinct real ticker/headline pairs: 30 ticker-balanced random, 30 year-balanced random, 60 targeted boundary cases; plus 20 synthetic regression cases.
method.reference_process: Two separate assistant reviews without model predictions; disagreement or ambiguous labels excluded from agreement metrics. References frozen before scoring.
method.policy: Infer unnamed recommendation membership only for uniformly directional recommendations matching target stock/ETF type; retain other-company, fund-vs-holding, sector and mixed-role guards.
method.selection: Nine configurations tested. The final five-example target-first prompt had 142/174 agreement versus 143/174 for six examples, with about 10% higher throughput; selected as the practical speed/accuracy compromise. Batch size four retained; the six-example batch comparison found eight slower.
limitations: Small nonrepresentative evaluation; rare negative and mixed cases have very low holdout support.
The expanded association policy differs from the baseline policy, so agreement gains include task alignment rather than solely improved accuracy.

Recommendation references use the association assumption; five article-body checks found three actual picks and two incidental/related-company mentions. These checks do not estimate a population error rate.
Assistant annotations are not independent human gold labels. This held-out sample becomes a regression set after this evaluation; future prompt development needs a new holdout.
Validation groups were later used for additional finalist comparisons; reported aggregate agreement is model-selection evidence, not an untouched independent final-test accuracy estimate.
method.followup_cases: 40 disjoint real cases: 20 random, 10 screened by prior negative prediction, 10 activity-list cases; two blind assistant reviews, 3 ambiguous/disagreed cases excluded.
